blocks.prompt: 3 (i) Prove the following identities: \(\dfrac{\sin 3x - \sin x}{\cos x - \cos 3x} = \cot 2x\)
blocks.explanation:
A fraction whose top and bottom are each a difference of two trig ratios.
We must show the L.H.S. equals \(\cot 2x\).
Plan: change the top and the bottom into products, cancel the common factors, and recognise \(\frac{\cos}{\sin} = \cot\).
steps:
Given: L.H.S. \(= \dfrac{\sin 3x - \sin x}{\cos x - \cos 3x}\).
To prove: L.H.S. \(= \cot 2x\).
Method: Sum-to-product formulas
\[\sin P - \sin Q = 2\cos\tfrac{P + Q}{2}\sin\tfrac{P - Q}{2}\]
\[\cos P - \cos Q = -2\sin\tfrac{P + Q}{2}\sin\tfrac{P - Q}{2}\]

Numerator as a product (\(P = 3x\), \(Q = x\))
\[\sin 3x - \sin x\]
\[= 2\cos 2x\sin x\]
Why: Half-sum \(\frac{4x}{2} = 2x\), half-difference \(\frac{2x}{2} = x\).

Denominator as a product (\(P = x\), \(Q = 3x\))
\[\cos x - \cos 3x\]
\[= -2\sin 2x\sin(-x)\]
\[= 2\sin 2x\sin x\]
Why: The half-difference is \(\frac{x - 3x}{2} = -x\), and \(\sin(-x) = -\sin x\), so the two minus signs make a plus.

Divide and cancel
\[\text{L.H.S.} = \dfrac{2\cos 2x\sin x}{2\sin 2x\sin x}\]
\[= \dfrac{\cos 2x}{\sin 2x}\]
\[= \cot 2x = \text{R.H.S.}\]
Why: \(2\sin x\) is a common factor of the top and the bottom (we assume \(\sin x \ne 0\)), and \(\frac{\cos}{\sin} = \cot\).

Check: \(x = 15^{\circ}\)
\[\dfrac{\sin 45^{\circ} - \sin 15^{\circ}}{\cos 15^{\circ} - \cos 45^{\circ}}\]
\[\approx \dfrac{0.4483}{0.2588}\]
\[\approx 1.732 = \cot 30^{\circ} \;\checkmark\]
Why: \(\cot 30^{\circ} = \sqrt{3} \approx 1.732\).

blocks.explanation:
Top: sum of sines; bottom: sum of cosines, with the same two angles.
We must show the fraction is \(\tan 5x\).
Plan: write both as products; the factor \(\cos 3x\) appears in both and cancels.
steps:
Given: L.H.S. \(= \dfrac{\sin 8x + \sin 2x}{\cos 8x + \cos 2x}\).
To prove: L.H.S. \(= \tan 5x\).
Method: Sum-to-product
\[\sin P + \sin Q = 2\sin\tfrac{P + Q}{2}\cos\tfrac{P - Q}{2}\]
\[\cos P + \cos Q = 2\cos\tfrac{P + Q}{2}\cos\tfrac{P - Q}{2}\]

Find the new angles (\(P = 8x\), \(Q = 2x\))
\[\dfrac{P + Q}{2} = 5x\]
\[\dfrac{P - Q}{2} = 3x\]
Why: Both top and bottom use the same \(P\) and \(Q\), so the angles are the same.

Write both as products
\[\sin 8x + \sin 2x = 2\sin 5x\cos 3x\]
\[\cos 8x + \cos 2x = 2\cos 5x\cos 3x\]
Why: The two formulas above with these angles.

Divide and cancel
\[\text{L.H.S.} = \dfrac{2\sin 5x\cos 3x}{2\cos 5x\cos 3x}\]
\[= \dfrac{\sin 5x}{\cos 5x}\]
\[= \tan 5x = \text{R.H.S.}\]
Why: \(2\cos 3x\) cancels (we assume it is not zero), and \(\frac{\sin}{\cos} = \tan\).

Check: \(x = 10^{\circ}\)
\[\dfrac{\sin 80^{\circ} + \sin 20^{\circ}}{\cos 80^{\circ} + \cos 20^{\circ}}\]
\[\approx \dfrac{1.3268}{1.1133}\]
\[\approx 1.1918 = \tan 50^{\circ} \;\checkmark\]
Why: Both sides agree.

blocks.prompt: 3 (iii) [printed as (ii)] Prove the following identities: \(\dfrac{\sin A - \sin B}{\sin A + \sin B} = \tan\dfrac{A - B}{2}\cot\dfrac{A + B}{2}\)
blocks.explanation:
The same idea with general angles \(A\) and \(B\): top is a difference, bottom a sum, of sines.
We must reach \(\tan\frac{A - B}{2}\cot\frac{A + B}{2}\).
Plan: write both as products, then group a \(\frac{\sin}{\cos}\) and a \(\frac{\cos}{\sin}\).
steps:
Given: L.H.S. \(= \dfrac{\sin A - \sin B}{\sin A + \sin B}\).
To prove: L.H.S. \(= \tan\frac{A - B}{2}\cot\frac{A + B}{2}\).
Method: Sum-to-product
\[\sin A - \sin B = 2\cos\tfrac{A + B}{2}\sin\tfrac{A - B}{2}\]
\[\sin A + \sin B = 2\sin\tfrac{A + B}{2}\cos\tfrac{A - B}{2}\]

Put the products in the fraction
\[\text{L.H.S.} = \dfrac{2\cos\frac{A + B}{2}\sin\frac{A - B}{2}}{2\sin\frac{A + B}{2}\cos\frac{A - B}{2}}\]
Why: These are exactly the two formulas with \(P = A\), \(Q = B\).

Cancel the 2 and regroup
\[= \dfrac{\sin\frac{A - B}{2}}{\cos\frac{A - B}{2}}\cdot\dfrac{\cos\frac{A + B}{2}}{\sin\frac{A + B}{2}}\]
Why: Put the two ratios with angle \(\frac{A - B}{2}\) together and the two with \(\frac{A + B}{2}\) together.

Recognise tan and cot
\[= \tan\dfrac{A - B}{2}\cot\dfrac{A + B}{2}\]
\[= \text{R.H.S.}\]
Why: \(\frac{\sin}{\cos} = \tan\) and \(\frac{\cos}{\sin} = \cot\).

Check: \(A = 90^{\circ}\), \(B = 30^{\circ}\)
\[\dfrac{1 - \tfrac{1}{2}}{1 + \tfrac{1}{2}} = \dfrac{1}{3}\]
\[\tan 30^{\circ}\cot 60^{\circ}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\cdot\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{1}{3} \;\checkmark\]
Why: Both sides equal \(\frac{1}{3}\).
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: \(\dfrac{\sin A - \sin B}{\sin A + \sin B} = \tan\dfrac{A - B}{2}\cot\dfrac{A + B}{2}\)

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book labels this third part "(ii)" a second time and has no part (iii); the parts read (i), (ii), (ii), (iv). It is part (iii) here. The identity itself is printed correctly.

blocks.explanation:
A fraction of fixed angles, like part (ii) but with numbers.
We must show it equals \(\sqrt{3}\).
Plan: write top and bottom as products; \(\cos 20^{\circ}\) cancels and \(\tan 60^{\circ} = \sqrt{3}\) is left.
steps:
Given: L.H.S. \(= \dfrac{\sin 80^{\circ} + \sin 40^{\circ}}{\cos 80^{\circ} + \cos 40^{\circ}}\).
To prove: L.H.S. \(= \sqrt{3}\).
Method: \(\sin P + \sin Q\) and \(\cos P + \cos Q\) formulas with \(P = 80^{\circ}\), \(Q = 40^{\circ}\). (The book prints the degree marks as small primes.)

Find the new angles
\[\dfrac{P + Q}{2} = \dfrac{120^{\circ}}{2} = 60^{\circ}\]
\[\dfrac{P - Q}{2} = \dfrac{40^{\circ}}{2} = 20^{\circ}\]
Why: Half-sum and half-difference.

Write both as products
\[\sin 80^{\circ} + \sin 40^{\circ} = 2\sin 60^{\circ}\cos 20^{\circ}\]
\[\cos 80^{\circ} + \cos 40^{\circ} = 2\cos 60^{\circ}\cos 20^{\circ}\]
Why: Sum-to-product formulas.

Divide and cancel
\[\text{L.H.S.} = \dfrac{2\sin 60^{\circ}\cos 20^{\circ}}{2\cos 60^{\circ}\cos 20^{\circ}}\]
\[= \tan 60^{\circ}\]
\[= \sqrt{3} = \text{R.H.S.}\]
Why: \(2\cos 20^{\circ} \ne 0\) cancels; \(\frac{\sin 60^{\circ}}{\cos 60^{\circ}} = \tan 60^{\circ} = \sqrt{3}\).

Check with a calculator
\[\dfrac{0.9848 + 0.6428}{0.1736 + 0.7660} = \dfrac{1.6276}{0.9397}\]
\[\approx 1.732 = \sqrt{3} \;\checkmark\]
Why: Both sides agree.
